blocking_findings.claim: "Every one of the 48,608 rank-point drops was the same inversion: the exact true pair added below an existing single allele of that pair. None had another cause." (line 48)
blocking_findings.why_wrong: False as a characterization of the measured space. In 36,456 cases (74.9%) the base file's scoring partial match was a wrong-partner PAIR row, not a single-allele row; only 12,152 had a single-allele partial. hedging_modes.py only checked 'added the exact true pair lower than an existing partial' (any partial row), so its 'unexplained: 0' never distinguished single from mixed partials.
blocking_findings.evidence: Independent re-enumeration, identical universe and arms (1,735,200 strict-below comparisons): rank_point_drops=48,608; base partial SINGLE: 12,152; base partial MIXED pair: 36,456; other: 0.

blocking_findings.why_wrong: Rule 2 guards only single rows, but 75% of measured drops come from a wrong-partner PAIR above the true pair, a shape Step 4 explicitly creates with three or more qualifying alleles in one gene. Nothing selects which pair takes row 1.
blocking_findings.evidence: evaluation.py lines 152-153 (full match taken unconditionally); classifier counts above.

blocking_findings.evidence: Line 72; Step 5 assigns EPCR by final row position, so every choice propagates into the score.
